correctness.rationale: Given stationary common-rate Poisson resetting, condition on exponential backward age and the event of no intervening reset (failure probability O(1/log N)); at fixed positive age each particle pair is bivariate normal with (1-rho_N)log N to s/(2a). Gaussian tails plus conditional regression prove the stated Hüsler–Reiss exceedance intensity. Empirical second-moment normalization contributes only O_P(log N/sqrt(N)). Bounded convergence yields the bivariate exponential-age mixture, Cauchy–Schwarz proves its strict non-max-stability, and an exact differentiated inverse-Gaussian integral yields exp(-sqrt(s)). Assumptions, positive parameters, ordered limits and endpoints are explicitly documented. The independently executable checker passed 82 numerical cross-checks; finite tests alone are not the proof.

(2022); the conditional critical-lag two-time Gaussian extreme-value law is covered by Le Doussal (2023). The new assessed claim is their model-specific combination after empirical-width normalization: the exact stationary exponential-age mixture of bivariate Hüsler–Reiss laws, strict non-max-stability of that mixture, and the evaluated universal ordered-limit tail coefficient exp(-sqrt(s)). Searches of related published findings and the accessible primary literature identified no equivalent evaluated common-reset self-normalized two-time extreme law. This is a qualified same-model finding, not proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: Common resetting introduces a latent renewal age shared by all particles. Empirical-width normalization produces universal Gumbel one-time extremes but leaves an analytically sharp temporal signature in their jointly observed edge; the conditional Gaussian max-stable process becomes a non-max-stable random-age mixture. The explicit exp(-sqrt(s)) law supplies a natural quantitative decorrelation scale for rare extreme-particle events and is structurally distinct from ordinary covariance or arbitrary finite slices; it is a motivated extension of established Brownian-gas extreme statistics.
